meta.description: Designs adaptive clinical trials including group-sequential, blinded and unblinded sample-size re-estimation, treatment selection, enrichment, response-adaptive randomisation, platform trials, dose finding, and current regulatory review boundaries.

scientific_integrity.detail: No retained output fabricated a trial result, sample size, p-value, efficacy claim, DOI, or PMID; numerical evidence came from exact candidate runs, bounded controls, or identified authoritative sources.

practice_boundaries.detail: The skill is framed as protocol and statistical design support rather than patient-specific diagnosis or prescribing, and it repeatedly requires pre-specification, IDMC separation, simulation, and regulatory verification.

methodological_ground.detail: The EXNEX-labelled section does not implement EXNEX detachment, the promising-zone section omits its adaptation and preserved-weight rule, and the blinded-SSR code makes an unconditional Type-I statement.

code_usability.detail: Three of seven executable candidate sections error, and the shipped full program stops at section 3 before later sections can run.

functional_suitability.note: The workflow covers the promised design families, but three executable sections fail and several named methods are only partial or conceptual implementations.

reliability.note: Package errors are visible, but the advertised full runner halts at the first defect and the supplied examples lack structured validation and recovery guidance.

performance_context.note: The main skill is concise and routes conditional detail into focused references and a single reusable script with little redundant loading.

agent_usability.note: The workflow, design-selection table, guardrails, and deliverables are unusually clear, but executable-versus-conceptual boundaries and failure feedback are not consistently surfaced at invocation time.

human_usability.note: Natural prompts and scenario tables are highly discoverable; users cannot recover cleanly from the current package-interface and shape errors without independent expertise.

security.note: There are no credentials, destructive operations, or raw-string execution paths; numeric design inputs are not programmatically validated before entering statistical APIs.

maintainability.note: References are modular and the script is sectioned, but no shipped regression harness locks package contracts, random seeds, or method-level assertions.

agent_specific.note: Trigger precision, progressive disclosure, composability, and stop conditions are strong; stochastic examples are not idempotent and runnable surfaces overstate some method coverage.

inputs.label: OBF survival design
inputs.note: Sections 1 and 2 ran successfully; independent controls reproduced sensible OBF boundaries, null crossing probability, events, and sample size.

assertions.text: The O'Brien-Fleming design executes on the exact candidate constants.
assertions.note: Section 1 completed and produced three efficacy boundaries.

assertions.text: The survival sample-size calculation executes and exposes accrual, dropout, follow-up, event, and subject assumptions.
assertions.note: Section 2 completed and printed 229.4 final events and about 449.4 subjects.

assertions.text: The independent control attains the one-sided null crossing probability near 0.025.
assertions.note: The retained control reported 0.025000000388.

assertions.text: The result remains tied to proportional-hazards assumptions and warns against using it unchanged for delayed effects.
assertions.note: The routed reference explicitly requires a non-PH method or simulation for delayed immunotherapy effects.

assertions.text: The candidate records installed-package compatibility expectations rather than silently assuming one version.
assertions.note: Version compatibility and help-page inspection are explicit in SKILL.md.

inputs.label: Blinded variance SSR
inputs.note: The fixed rpact design errors before either sample-size calculation because asUser lacks userAlphaSpending; a valid current fixed-design control proves the intended SD comparison is otherwise available.

assertions.text: The exact section executes through both the SD 12 and SD 14 sample-size calls.
assertions.note: rpact 4.4.0 stops while constructing design_initial.

assertions.text: The valid current-interface control shows higher blinded SD increases required sample size.
assertions.note: The control increased total subjects from 182.78 to 248.08.

assertions.text: The implementation clearly distinguishes nuisance-only blinded recalculation from an unblinded treatment-effect adaptation.
assertions.note: The prose and section heading identify blinded pooled-SD re-estimation.

assertions.text: The Type-I claim is conditional and tied to the implemented final test and recalculation rule.
assertions.note: The script states Type-I error is not affected without conditions or a matching simulation.

assertions.text: Failure output gives a candidate-level recovery action.
assertions.note: Only the raw rpact missing-userAlphaSpending error is emitted.

inputs.label: Promising-zone combination design

assertions.text: The current rpact inverse-normal design constructs with the declared information rates and spending.
assertions.note: Section 4 completed without warnings or errors.

assertions.text: The candidate warns that naive unblinded sample-size increases inflate Type-I error.
assertions.note: This is a non-negotiable guardrail in the main skill and reference.

assertions.text: The candidate presents 30% to 80% as an example design choice rather than a universal default.
assertions.note: The reference explicitly says these thresholds are design choices.

assertions.text: The executable computes conditional power and applies the promising-zone increase up to a specified n_max.
assertions.note: Those steps appear only as comments and n_max is absent.

assertions.text: The executable demonstrates preserved original weights and calibrated Type-I error.
assertions.note: No CHW weight application or null simulation is performed.

assertions.text: The exact BOIN boundary call executes for target 0.30, ten cohorts, and cohort size three.
assertions.note: Section 5 completed and returned escalation and de-escalation boundaries.

assertions.text: The exact six-dose operating-characteristic simulation executes and returns MTD selection and expected sample size.
assertions.note: The run returned six selection percentages and expected N 26.961.

assertions.text: An independent seeded control confirms the package and input family produce a valid reproducible result.

assertions.note: The platform reference includes this exact qualification.

assertions.text: The shipped simulation itself records a seed and avoids implying that FDA generally prefers BOIN.

assertions.note: map_prior is created before the subsequent error.

inputs.label: Run all shipped adaptive examples
inputs.note: The full program executes sections 1 and 2 then stops at section 3; sections 7, 9, and 10 are responsibly comments-only but cannot be treated as finished SAP implementations.

assertions.text: The full shipped script exits successfully after all ten sections.
assertions.note: It exits 1 at section 3.

assertions.text: Sections 7, 9, and 10 are visibly identified as conceptual scaffolds rather than silently masquerading as executions.
assertions.note: The code contains comments only and SKILL.md calls conceptual sections scaffolds.

assertions.text: Restricted commercial tools are not bypassed or represented as locally validated.
assertions.note: East, ADDPLAN, and FACTS are only documented and the tooling classifies them as restricted.

assertions.text: The full runner preserves later independent evidence after an earlier section fails.
assertions.note: Ordinary R sourcing terminates at the first error.

assertions.text: Every named implementation produces SAP-ready boundaries, rules, simulations, and bias controls.
assertions.note: Enrichment, graduation, and RAR remain conceptual only and multiple executable methods are partial or broken.

key_strengths: The normalized package preserves MIT provenance and separates a concise core workflow from method-specific and regulatory references.
The design-selection table and non-negotiable guardrails correctly distinguish blinded from unblinded SSR, discourage two-arm RAR by default, and require selection-bias correction.
Group-sequential O'Brien-Fleming and survival examples execute successfully and agree with independently asserted current-package controls.
Conceptual and restricted surfaces are explicitly labelled, and the skill requires authoritative status checks before regulatory claims.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-001: Repair the blinded SSR design
recommendations.problem: The shipped program stops while constructing the fixed rpact design because typeOfDesign asUser lacks required user alpha spending.
recommendations.root_cause: A group-sequential asUser constructor is being used for a fixed final-analysis blinded-SSR example without its mandatory spending contract.
recommendations.fix: Use the current supported fixed-design contract, remove ignored or incompatible arguments, execute both SD scenarios, and add an assertion that the higher nuisance variance increases sample size while the prespecified final test remains unchanged.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-002: Align and validate CRM dose grids
recommendations.problem: The CRM example passes six true probabilities with a five-dose skeleton, returns a malformed object, and fails during printing.
recommendations.root_cause: The example lacks a preflight invariant requiring the true curve, skeleton, and dose labels to have identical lengths.
recommendations.fix: Provide a calibrated six-dose skeleton or reduce the true curve to five doses, reject dimension mismatches before simulation, set a seed, and assert the returned selection and allocation schema before comparison with BOIN.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-003: Implement EXNEX or relabel MAP
recommendations.problem: The EXNEX-labelled example fits a single MAP model, fails to convert it before ESS, and has no non-exchangeable stratum component.
recommendations.root_cause: A simplified historical MAP snippet was presented as a basket EXNEX implementation and uses a stale RBesT density contract.
recommendations.fix: Either implement an actual stratum-level EXNEX or robust mixture with explicit exchangeability weights and conflict sensitivity, or relabel the section as a MAP-prior demonstration. For ESS, use the current gMAP to mixture-fit conversion and test the resulting density.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-004: Make stochastic examples reproducible
recommendations.problem: BOIN, CRM, and Bayesian examples do not set or report seeds, so operating characteristics and fitted mixture approximations can change between runs.
recommendations.root_cause: The script treats simulation as an illustrative side effect rather than a versioned reproducible deliverable.
recommendations.fix: Set named seeds before every stochastic surface, record replicate counts and package versions with outputs, and add deterministic schema and tolerance assertions rather than locking incidental Monte Carlo values.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-005: Complete the promising-zone rule
recommendations.problem: The section labelled Mehta-Pocock with CHW weights only constructs a base inverse-normal design and sample size.
recommendations.root_cause: Conditional power, the adaptation function, maximum sample size, original-weight preservation, and null calibration were left as comments.
recommendations.fix: Implement and pre-specify the conditional-power zones, n_max, original weights, stagewise statistic, and IDMC output. Simulate null and alternative operating characteristics with Monte Carlo uncertainty, or clearly mark the entire section documented-only.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-006: Qualify the blinded SSR Type-I claim
recommendations.problem: The code says Type-I error is not affected solely because the test ignores SSR, while the main reference correctly uses conditional language.
recommendations.root_cause: An illustrative comment collapses the assumptions needed for nuisance-only blinded re-estimation to preserve the final test.
recommendations.fix: State the exact conditions: blinded nuisance estimation, a prespecified rule, unchanged valid final test, and no treatment-effect leakage. Add a bounded null simulation or cite the supported design contract and avoid an unconditional guarantee.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-007: Remove the FDA preference claim
recommendations.problem: The code comment says the pre-tabulated table is why FDA prefers BOIN.
recommendations.root_cause: A Fit-for-Purpose determination was paraphrased as broad regulatory preference.
recommendations.fix: Say that FDA issued a Fit-for-Purpose determination for the BOIN method in December 2021 and retain the existing warning that each proposed trial still requires calibration and review.

recommendations.title: ADAPT-008: Refresh regulatory status routing
recommendations.problem: The regulatory reference does not mention FDA's June 2026 broader revised draft for master protocols and uses the June 2025 ICH milestone without distinguishing FDA's September 2025 draft issue date.
recommendations.root_cause: The source snapshot was frozen before the later FDA updates, while the skill is intended for current reviewer-facing work.
recommendations.fix: Add the June 2026 broader draft alongside the still-final March 2022 oncology guidance, record access dates, and distinguish ICH Step 2 endorsement from the later FDA draft-publication date.
